\chapter{A Secret Found Out}
\label{ch:ml-a-secret-found-out}
\hlchaptermodality{383}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say a secret, to appear, to vanish, to find out and to retrieve.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 383: I can say a secret, to appear, to vanish, to find out and to retrieve.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{രഹസ്യം} (rahasyaṁ)}{രഹസ്യം (rahasyaṁ)}]{\ml{രഹസ്യം} (rahasyaṁ) — a secret}

\label{lesson:ML-C383-rahasyam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to drive away, then the Malayalam for to calm down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{രഹസ്യം}}
\textbf{\ml{രഹസ്യം}} — \emph{rahasyaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a secret\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൾ} \ml{ആ} \ml{രഹസ്യം} \ml{ആരോടും} \ml{പറഞ്ഞില്ല}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷ ā rahasyaṁ ārōṭuṁ paṟaññilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She told nobody that secret.
\end{quote}

Secretly is \ml{രഹസ്യമായി}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{രഹസ്യം}} (\emph{rahasyaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{rahasya}, \textquotedblleft{}private, secret\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10669).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rahasyaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rahasyaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaḷ ā rahasyaṁ ārōṭuṁ paṟaññilla.} — She told nobody that secret.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to drive away, then the Malayalam for to calm down, then say \emph{rahasyaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{രഹസ്യം} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A secret\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക} (pratyakṣappeṭuka)}{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക (pratyakṣappeṭuka)}]{\ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക} (pratyakṣappeṭuka) — to appear; to show up}

\label{lesson:ML-C383-pratyaksappetuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to calm down, then the Malayalam for a secret.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക}}
\textbf{\ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക}} — \emph{pratyakṣappeṭuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to appear; to show up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{മഴയ്ക്ക്} \ml{ശേഷം} \ml{ആകാശത്തിൽ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{മഴവില്ല്} \ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെട്ടു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻaykkŭ śēṣaṁ ākāśattil oru maḻavillŭ pratyakṣappeṭṭu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the rain a rainbow appeared in the sky.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെട്ടു}, \emph{pratyakṣappeṭṭu}.

\ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷം}, before the eyes, + -\ml{പ്പെടുക}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക}} (\emph{pratyakṣappeṭuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{pratyakṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}visible, present before the eyes\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8635), with -\ml{പ്പെടുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to come to be\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratyakṣappeṭuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratyakṣappeṭuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maḻaykkŭ śēṣaṁ ākāśattil oru maḻavillŭ pratyakṣappeṭṭu.} — After the rain a rainbow appeared in the sky.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to calm down, then the Malayalam for a secret, then say \emph{pratyakṣappeṭuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പ്രത്യക്ഷപ്പെടുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To appear; to show up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മറയുക} (maṟayuka)}{മറയുക (maṟayuka)}]{\ml{മറയുക} (maṟayuka) — to vanish; to go out of sight}

\label{lesson:ML-C383-marayuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a secret, then the Malayalam for to appear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{മറയുക}}
\textbf{\ml{മറയുക}} — \emph{maṟayuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to vanish; to go out of sight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{സൂര്യൻ} \ml{കുന്നിന്റെ} \ml{പിന്നിൽ} \ml{മറഞ്ഞു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sūryan kunninṟe pinnil maṟaññu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sun vanished behind the hill.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{മറഞ്ഞു}, \emph{maṟaññu}.

To go behind something and out of sight.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{മറയുക}} (\emph{maṟayuka}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 4760 lists Malayalam \emph{maṟayuka}, \textquotedblleft{}to disappear, to hide oneself\textquotedblright{}, with \ml{മറ}, \textquotedblleft{}a screen, a cover\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṟayuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maṟayuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sūryan kunninṟe pinnil maṟaññu.} — The sun vanished behind the hill.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for a secret, then the Malayalam for to appear, then say \emph{maṟayuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{മറയുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To vanish; to go out of sight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക} (kaṇṭupiṭikkuka)}{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക (kaṇṭupiṭikkuka)}]{\ml{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക} (kaṇṭupiṭikkuka) — to find out; to discover}

\label{lesson:ML-C383-kantupitikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to appear, then the Malayalam for to vanish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക}} — \emph{kaṇṭupiṭikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to find out; to discover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പോലീസ്} \ml{ആ} \ml{മോഷണത്തിന്റെ} \ml{രഹസ്യം} \ml{കണ്ടുപിടിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pōlīsŭ ā mōṣaṇattinṟe rahasyaṁ kaṇṭupiṭiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police found out the secret of that theft.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കണ്ടുപിടിച്ചു}, \emph{kaṇṭupiṭiccu}.

Also to invent: \ml{ആരാണ്} \ml{ഫോൺ} \ml{കണ്ടുപിടിച്ചത്}? Who invented the telephone?

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക}} (\emph{kaṇṭupiṭikkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കണ്ട്}, \textquotedblleft{}having seen\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{കാണുക} (\emph{kāṇuka}) (DEDR 1443), and \ml{പിടിക്കുക} (\emph{piṭikkuka}), \textquotedblleft{}to catch\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4148): to see and catch hold of.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṇṭupiṭikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṇṭupiṭikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pōlīsŭ ā mōṣaṇattinṟe rahasyaṁ kaṇṭupiṭiccu.} — The police found out the secret of that theft.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to appear, then the Malayalam for to vanish, then say \emph{kaṇṭupiṭikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{കണ്ടുപിടിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To find out; to discover\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കണ്ടെടുക്കുക} (kaṇṭeṭukkuka)}{കണ്ടെടുക്കുക (kaṇṭeṭukkuka)}]{\ml{കണ്ടെടുക്കുക} (kaṇṭeṭukkuka) — to retrieve; to recover}

\label{lesson:ML-C383-kantetukkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to vanish, then the Malayalam for to find out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കണ്ടെടുക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{കണ്ടെടുക്കുക}} — \emph{kaṇṭeṭukkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to retrieve; to recover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പോലീസ്} \ml{മോഷ്ടിച്ച} \ml{സ്വർണ്ണം} \ml{കണ്ടെടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pōlīsŭ mōṣṭicca svarṇṇaṁ kaṇṭeṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police recovered the stolen gold.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{കണ്ടെടുത്തു}, \emph{kaṇṭeṭuttu}.

\ml{കണ്ട്}, having found, + \ml{എടുക്കുക}, to take: found and taken back.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കണ്ടെടുക്കുക}} (\emph{kaṇṭeṭukkuka}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{കണ്ട്}, \textquotedblleft{}having seen, having found\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{കാണുക} (DEDR 1443), and \ml{എടുക്കുക} (\emph{eṭukkuka}), \textquotedblleft{}to take up\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 851).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṇṭeṭukkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pōlīsŭ mōṣṭicca svarṇṇaṁ kaṇṭeṭuttu.} — The police recovered the stolen gold.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to vanish, then the Malayalam for to find out, then say \emph{kaṇṭeṭukkuka} again
\end{itemize}
